_comment: AC-REL-04: pinned SBOM tooling for the published image + host binaries. Config only — CI wires it in two places, both BLOCKING for generation: .github/workflows/publish.yml (job `provenance`, scanning the PUBLISHED image by manifest digest and asserting the SBOM is non-empty and that the image it records is the published index or one of its platform children) and .github/workflows/legal.yml (job `sbom`, scanning the repo tree on every PR). What is still NOT implemented, and is claimed nowhere, is SBOM DIFFING as a release gate — see docs/legal/FINDINGS.md #7.
actionRefVerifiedVia: resolved from the repo's own tag list via `gh api repos/docker/scout-action/commits/v1.9.3`, not a moving major tag. Replaced anchore/sbom-action, whose first act is to download the syft binary from a third-party release CDN: that download returned 503 twice in one afternoon, once in legal.yml and once in publish.yml, where it failed a release whose every other gate was green. Scout is Docker's own tool and ships in the Docker CLI.

targets.note: pinned by digest, not tag: the tag is mutable, the digest is the artifact that was published. Scout resolves a multi-arch reference to the PLATFORM CHILD it analyzes and records THAT digest in the pkg:oci purl, so the assertion accepts the index digest or any of its children.

licensePolicyReuse: scripts/legal/notices-policy.json — the SAME fail-closed allowedClasses/weakCopyleftAllowlist gate applies to whatever Scout reports; no separate, drifting policy.

provenance.invariant: a published version's image digest is immutable once recorded — verify-provenance.sh fails closed on any attempt to re-record a DIFFERENT digest for the same version. It is wired in publish.yml's `provenance` job, which runs AFTER the `merge` job assembles the multi-arch manifest and exports its digest (`docker buildx imagetools inspect`) as a job output.
provenance.scopeLimit: the immutability check compares against a PRIOR record. In CI each run starts from a clean workspace and uploads the record as an artifact, so cross-run uniqueness comes from the `version` job only ever selecting an unused v<version> tag — see docs/legal/FINDINGS.md.
